items.text: Control of the House and Senate is on the ballot; polls are starting to close and results will become clear overnight and tomorrow. As of the morning, prediction markets gave Democrats about a 76% chance of winning both chambers; JPMorgan warned of short-term volatility depending on the outcome.
items.title: US midterm elections today

items.text: Iran said it could reopen the strait within 48 hours if its terms are met, and otherwise it stays closed; the sides remain far apart on the Qatar-brokered draft deal. The US carried out a limited "defensive" strike on Qeshm island overnight. This is the number-one risk for oil and inflation expectations.
items.title: US–Iran: Hormuz still closed

items.text: The US 10-year yield rose to 4.95%. September JOLTS job openings beat expectations at 7.52 million, but hiring is weak; Wednesday's Treasury quarterly refunding announcement is key for auction sizes.
items.title: Yields climb

items.text: The US, Russia and Ukraine are scheduled to meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11. Meanwhile, a Russian strike on an aid distribution point killed at least 29 people, and Ukrainian drones hit the Yaroslavl refinery.
items.title: Ukraine peace talks

items.text: AMD beat expectations with data-center revenue up about 97% and rose about 7% after the close. Apple and Palantir fell despite beating; Shopify dropped sharply after missing on revenue.
items.title: Earnings
